strategy_title: Add num_warps=2 configs to reduce warp scheduler contention
strategy_description: When a Triton autotune config set lacks small num_warps options (e.g., num_warps=2) and the CPIStall 'not-selected' metric is high (>25% of cycles), adding configs with fewer warps per block reduces scheduler contention and lowers Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction. The effective block size selected at runtime dropped from 128 to 64 threads (num_warps=2), reducing Active Warps Per Scheduler from 11.19 to 6.81 and cutting Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 15.84 to 13.62, yielding a ~5% latency reduction. This is most beneficial for compute-bound kernels dominated by integer/ALU operations where warp-level parallelism exceeds what the scheduler can efficiently arbitrate.
applicable_when: Triton autotune config set has no num_warps=2 entries; CPIStall 'not-selected' stall is >25% of total warp cycles; kernel is ALU/integer-heavy (SM Busy >60% on active cycles); Active Warps Per Scheduler is high (>8); kernel does not rely on high occupancy to hide memory latency
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is memory-latency-bound (DRAM throughput >50%) where high occupancy is needed to hide latency; grid is already under 1 full wave (waves_per_sm < 1.0) and reducing block size would further reduce parallelism; kernel uses shared memory heavily where fewer warps per block reduces reuse
framework_notes: Triton-specific: num_warps controls warps per block in the autotune config. Adding num_warps=2 configs allows the autotuner to select 64-thread blocks (2 warps × 32 threads). Equivalent in CUDA would be launching with blockDim.x=64. The autotuner selects the best config at benchmark time, so adding configs only helps if the smaller warp count genuinely wins.
